topics.title: The AI copyright reckoning everyone keeps postponing just got a date.
topics.why: Andersen v. Stability AI has a summary-judgment hearing set for Nov. 4 and the OpenAI MDL's reply briefs are due Nov. 6 — the cases that decide whether training on copyrighted work is fair use are finally close enough to matter.

topics.title: The FDA just finished asking the public how to regulate AI doctors — and almost nobody noticed.
topics.why: The agency's comment period on agentic, generative-AI medical devices closed Oct. 19, right after a record 2025 of 295 AI/ML device clearances — the rulebook for AI in your doctor's office is being written in public right now.

topics.title: Doctors and lawyers in China are moonlighting as $15-an-hour AI trainers — the same jobs are opening up everywhere else.
topics.why: Data-annotation demand on Upwork is up 154% year over year and LinkedIn ranks it a top-4 fastest-growing U.S. job — the hidden gig economy behind every model release is now a real income stream for skilled professionals, not just click-workers.

topics.title: Twenty new AI models shipped this month and almost no one read a single release note.
topics.why: October alone has brought a confirmed 20 releases from 16 providers — Grok Voice 3.0, Nemotron 3.5, Jais 3, LFM2.5 — and the sheer volume is itself the story: picking tools by name recognition stopped working a while ago.

topics.title: Courts are now making lawyers swear, in writing, that they checked the AI.
topics.why: October rulings are piling up Rule 11 certification requirements and sanctions for fake AI-generated citations — the legal system's patience for 'the model made it up' is visibly running out this month.
